Plan and organize

Connect work items, Epics, and repository knowledge.

Start from a work item

Open Work items and choose Local, GitHub issues, or Jira.

  1. Choose Local → New and add context and acceptance criteria. It stays on your Mac.
  2. Start development on a Local item immediately starts the configured agent. GitHub and Jira items open a prepared composer for you to review and send.
  3. Open the item to follow tasks, PRs, and history. In an Epic, select a card to zoom in; Escape returns to the Epic.
  4. To publish an item, use Push to remote…, inspect the preview, then create the GitHub issue or Jira ticket. Conversations and local history are not included.

If publication is uncertain, link the existing remote item before retrying.

In a Local item's Context, choose Link work item to reference another Local item, GitHub issue, or Jira ticket in the workspace. Linked titles open their details; Unlink removes only the reference. Agents can create and read these links too. Use Epic membership for subtasks and dependencies for blockers.

Organize an Epic

An Epic groups work items, their development attempts, and dependencies in ByteQuay. A Local work item, GitHub issue, or Jira ticket can be an Epic. Its designation and work assignments stay on your Mac; a Local Epic does not need a published issue or ticket.

  1. Open a work item and choose Mark as Epic, then open its Work view. For GitHub or Jira Epics, review offered source children before Sync.
  2. Add a Local item, Add existing, or Suggest work. Inspect suggestions before Accept as Local.
  3. Use Planned, Working, and Done to track progress. Run on eligible work starts its development task immediately.
  4. Review outcomes, then Conclude Epic. Closing the source issue or ticket is separate.

Build repository memory

  1. Open Memory → Learn from my PRs, or choose Learn from this PR on a closed or merged PR.
  2. Inspect Rules, Recipes, and Specs, including their scope and sources. Edit, delete, or restore entries as needed.
  3. Choose whether agents use memory in Reviews, Development tasks, or both. Review entries under Needs you.

For a specification check, choose Memory → Check against spec, select the code and source pages, and start a ready agent. Inspect reproduced failures under Spec checks; Open local work item continues a finding. Unreproduced candidates stay separate.

Follow a Circle

Choose Circles → Create a circle, name it, and select people and optional repositories. Use Needs you, Activity, Members, and Insights to follow their work.

Creating a Circle sends no invitations. Refresh activity updates collected information; insights reflect that coverage, not a complete measure of a person’s work.

Learn with Artifacts

  1. Open Artifacts in a workspace and ask in Ask about this repository.
  2. The agent answers from the code, citing files by path and line, and ends each answer with a question card for what to look at next. Pick an option, or write your own reply.
  3. When nothing is left open, it offers a page. Choose Make the page, or Not yet to keep talking. You can also ask for a page at any time.
  4. The page opens beside the conversation. Ask for changes in the same conversation; each save adds a version under Versions.

The agent reads the repository but never changes it. A page’s buttons and quizzes work inside the page, which reaches nothing outside it.
